defect.summary: `readers.sig.clockToleranceMs` is ONE declared field governing TWO legs, and only ONE of them can report its distance to it. F3 carries `f3Deviation` on SigResult — maxDeclaredInversionMs, clockToleranceMs, distanceMs, pairsCompared — so `/explain` prints Sig's margin as a number. F1 does not. MEASURED AT BYTES 2026-09-29, in runF1: `const delta = prev.timestamp - curr.timestamp; if (delta > tolerance) { findings.push(...) }`. The gap is computed for EVERY adjacent pair and RETAINED ONLY WHEN IT ALREADY EXCEEDS THE TOLERANCE. So on a run that produces no finding there is no number anywhere — not on the result object, not in the decision, not on any surface — and no operator and no seat can state F1's distance to the line it is measured against. THIS IS THE REPAIR F3 ALREADY GOT AND F1 DID NOT: T3 item (4)'s own comment, four lines above F3's accumulator, reads "the largest deviation, kept as a NUMBER. It was always computed here and then survived only inside the finding's prose; recovering it meant parsing a reader's English for a number the reader already had." That sentence still describes runF1 exactly. FIX: an `f1Deviation` accumulator on SigResult in T3(4)'s shape, so a run that produces no finding still reports its headroom.
defect.ground: Frank's ruling, 2026-09-29, 'the clock tolerance: 3 then 2' — option 2, to be signed after Act B'. The build seat's measurement of the same day (ARC_MICA-NOTE_Two-Axis-Clock-Measurement_20260929.md): axis 2 reports -14 ms over the whole chain; axis 1 reports nothing, by construction. Declaration S13 returns the tolerance to 0 and its basis states, in the arbiter's words, that one axis is measured and the other is argued from the writer's construction rather than from its record.

arbiter.word: I, the arbiter, grant T9: Sig's F1 leg reports its largest measured inversion on every reading, silent or not, so that the record's agreement with itself shows its headroom and not only its breaches; granted because a reader that keeps a number only when it already exceeds the line cannot tell me how close it came.

conditions: PRE-REGISTRATION, WRITTEN BEFORE ANY CODE. `runF1` accumulates the largest `prev.timestamp - curr.timestamp` over its scope and returns it, and `assessSig` carries it onto SigResult as `f1Deviation` in EXACTLY `f3Deviation`'s shape: { maxDeclaredInversionMs, clockToleranceMs, distanceMs, pairsCompared }. `distanceMs` is `maxDeclaredInversionMs - clockToleranceMs`, so POSITIVE IS THE ADVERSE SIDE and negative is the headroom — identical in sign convention to F3, because two fields that mean the same thing and differ in sign are worse than one field.

NULL WHERE F3 IS NULL, AND FOR THE SAME REASONS. `f1Deviation` is null when F1 took no measurement: an unreadable log, a scope of fewer than two entries (no adjacent pair exists, so there is nothing to be a maximum OF), or a tolerance that was not injected as a finite non-negative number. It is NOT null merely because F1 found nothing — that case is the whole point of this ticket, and it must carry a number.

THE NUMBER IS THE READER'S, TAKEN WHERE IT IS COMPUTED. The accumulator lives inside runF1's existing loop, beside the comparison that already computes `delta`. It is NOT recomputed in assessSig, NOT derived from the findings' prose, and NOT reconstructed by a second pass over the entries. A second pass could disagree with the first if the scope were ever filtered differently, and a number that can disagree with the finding beside it is worse than no number.

WHAT A FAIL LOOKS LIKE, pre-registered: (a) a SILENT F1 over a non-empty scope still reports no deviation; (b) the sign convention differs from f3Deviation's, in either field; (c) the maximum is computed over a different scope than the findings are, so `pairsCompared` and the finding count can describe different sets; (d) `f1Deviation` is non-null when F1 took no measurement at all; (e) the twenty frozen scenarios move (this ticket does not open verdict-logic.frozen.json and must not need it); (f) any of the five src/mica suites returns other than 0 failed; (g) the door reports drift on any file not in `opens`.

THE `opens` LIST WAS MEASURED, NOT DESIGNED, AND THAT IS T8's LESSON APPLIED. T8 was signed with three files and broke nine tests in two more; the door went GREEN on that, because it compares digests and those files were not being changed, and what caught it was a sentence in the ticket. So this list was produced by MAKING THE CHANGE AS A PROBE AND RUNNING THE SUITES: with a purely additive field, ALL NINE pinned sig-adjacent suites passed unchanged — sig 57/57, sig-f3-clerk 46/46, substrate-snapshot 47/47, export 83/83, chokepoint 60/60, sig-f2-activation 19/19, sig-f2-reentry 14/14, sig-f2-d24-coverage 12/12, sig-f4-probe 37/37 — and the probe was then REVERTED. `sig.test.ts` is opened NOT because the change breaks it but because THE NEW TESTS BELONG IN IT: F1 has no test file of its own, and a ticket that could not add its own acceptance tests would be unverifiable.

SCOPE REFUSED, DELIBERATELY, AND NAMED SO IT IS NOT AN OVERSIGHT: this ticket does NOT open `src/mica/export/index.ts` or `src/mica/export.test.ts`. Printing F1's deviation in the export artifact beside F3's 'ORDER DEVIATION' block is the obvious next thing and it is a SEPARATE ticket. The reason is T8's other half: a too-small opens list costs a signature, and a too-large one grants authority nobody is using. Surfacing the number on `/explain` needs NO ticket at all — `sigMarginOf` is in `src/glue/wire.ts`, outside the door — and ships in the same commit round beside this one.

CODEX ACCEPTANCE: verify at committed bytes that a SILENT F1 over a scope of two or more entries reports a finite `maxDeclaredInversionMs`; that the sign convention matches `f3Deviation` field for field; that the accumulator and the findings walk THE SAME pairs (construct a scope where they could differ and show they do not); that no frozen scenario moved; and that the number cannot be obtained by parsing a finding's prose, because on a clean run there is no prose to parse. The build seat has been wrong repeatedly on this code and each time it was caught by an adversarial read, not by care.

DIGEST-PROVEN RELAY: the core change, its tests and the repin ship in ONE commit (npx ts-node src/core-door/core-door.ts --propose-repin T9-f1-reports-its-headroom), the glue suite prints the core door GREEN, and the committed bytes are what runs. The `sigMarginOf` change is NOT behind this door and ships as its own commit.
